walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An organism with two different alleles at a locus is:
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Hemizygous
Polyploid

mcqs.q: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes Aa × Aa gives a phenotypic ratio (dominance) of:
How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.

mcqs.q: What actually changes during natural selection in a population?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
The frequencies of alleles in the population's gene pool change across generations.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Individual organisms change their own genes to adapt.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gene”?
options: Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Heterozygous”?
options: Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Allele”?
options: Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Homozygous”?
options: Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Phenotype”?
options: Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Natural selection”?
options: Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.

free_texts.q: Type the key term that means: "Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic."
free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.
